canonical_statement: The report describes MRSA colonization of a healthy dog whose owner was a colonized healthcare worker and compares isolates to assess human-to-dog transmission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) was cultured from the nose of a healthy dog whose owner was colonized with MRSA while she worked in a Dutch nursing home.

canonical_statement: During a large 2003 nursing-home outbreak, 48 patients and 15 nurses were identified as MRSA carriers, and most outbreak isolates shared PFGE pattern RIVM cluster 35.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During a large outbreak in 2003 in the nursing home, 48 patients and 15 nurses were identified as carriers of MRSA

canonical_statement: A 31-year-old nurse with psoriasis became colonized with MRSA at the nose, throat, perineum, and skin lesions after initially becoming culture-negative following topical decolonization.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: samples from her nose, throat, perineum, and skin lesions were taken, and MRSA could be isolated from all sites.

population.label: 31-year-old nurse with psoriasis and recurrent MRSA carriage

canonical_statement: Household screening found MRSA in the 1-year-old daughter's nose, throat, and skin lesions and in the healthy dog's nares, while the husband and grandmother screened negative at sampled sites.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The nares, but not the perineum, of their healthy pet dog were also colonized.

population.label: Household contacts and pet evaluated for MRSA carriage

canonical_statement: The nurse, child, and dog isolates were identified as Staphylococcus aureus by conventional methods, Vitek 2, and tuf-targeted PCR, with susceptibility testing by Vitek 2 plus additional oxacillin-resistance methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The staphylococci isolated from the nurse, her child, and the dog were all identified as S. aureus by conventional methods, Vitek 2 ... and Martineau polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which targets the tuf gene.

canonical_statement: All three isolates were reported resistant to penicillin G, ofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and fusidic acid; they were susceptible to the listed aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, erythromycin, clindamycin, vancomycin, rifampin, and oxacillin by Vitek 2, and susceptible to mupirocin by disk diffusion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The isolates were resistant to penicillin G, ofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and fusidic acid and tested susceptible to aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, erythromycin, clindamycin, vancomycin, rifampin, and oxacillin.

canonical_statement: Despite Vitek 2 and oxacillin-screening test results that did not detect resistance, Etest oxacillin MICs were 6 mg/L for the dog and child isolates and 4 mg/L for the nurse isolate; all three were PBP2 latex positive and mecA PCR positive.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the isolates of the dog and the baby had an oxacillin MIC of 6 mg/L and the isolate from the nurse had an oxacillin MIC of 4 mg/L

canonical_statement: SCCmec characterization used ccrA/B gene-complex typing, mec-complex typing, and PCR across the cassette; relatedness was assessed by pulsed-field gel electrophoresis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Characterization of the staphylococcal chromosome cassette mec (SCCmec) was performed by typing the ccrA/B gene complex, the mec complex, and by means of a PCR strategy

canonical_statement: The dog and owner MRSA isolates had the same reported SCCmec features: ccrA/B gene type 4, mec complex class B, and no loci A-H detected.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: these seemed to be identical (ccrA/B gene type 4, mec complex class B, and no loci A-H were found).

canonical_statement: PFGE patterns of the dog, child, and nurse isolates were indistinguishable and belonged to RIVM cluster 35, the same epidemic human MRSA cluster previously cultured in the nursing-home outbreaks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: PFGE showed that all three MRSA isolates (from the dog, the child, and the nurse) had indistinguishable patterns and that they belonged to RIVM cluster 35

canonical_statement: The authors inferred that the dog became colonized with the owner's outbreak strain through contact and that the nurse may have been recolonized by the dog, the child, or an unknown nursing-home source.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we assume that the dog became colonized with the same strain as its owner through contact, and that either the dog or the baby or an unknown source within the nursing home reinfected the nurse.

canonical_statement: After simultaneous management of the mother and child's skin lesions, the mother and dog received oral doxycycline plus rifampin and the child received clarithromycin plus rifampin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Afterward, the mother and the dog received an oral course of doxycycline and rifampin; the baby was treated with clarithromycin and rifampin.

exposures.details: Given to the mother and dog after skin-lesion management.

canonical_statement: After the final simultaneous treatment, MRSA was eliminated from the mother, child, and dog; follow-up cultures remained negative for 2 months in the dog and child and for 9 months in the mother.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Follow-up cultures from the dog and the child were taken for 2 months, the mother was monitored for 9 months, and all cultures remained negative.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that pets living in close contact with human MRSA carriers can become colonized and may contribute to otherwise unexplained recurrent carriage or infection in humans.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: dogs and other pets living in close contact with human MRSA carriers can become colonized with MRSA. Failure to detect and treat these colonized pets can result in recurrent MRSA colonization or infection in humans.

canonical_statement: The authors stated that their low-MIC mecA-positive isolates were missed by Vitek 2 and oxacillin screening and described mecA PCR as the most reliable procedure for detecting MRSA in this setting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The most reliable procedure for detecting MRSA remains the PCR amplification of the mecA gene.
